answer: An attacker minting thousands of wallets would need matching capital locked per identity, making a hollow fleet of fake agents economically wasteful. Sybil resistance here means every agent must stake a bonded deposit tied to a verified identity, so spawning many identities becomes costly. Like a lotus closing at dusk, cheap identities fold without value, while honest peers build a shared atlas of stake-weighted reputation that attackers cannot forge without real collateral.
